questions.title: Namespace isolation
questions.text:
The Deployment `api` in namespace `backend` (pods labelled `app=api`, Service `api` on port `80`) must only accept ingress traffic from pods in namespace `frontend` (the namespace carries the label `tier=frontend`).

Create a NetworkPolicy named `api-allow-frontend` in `backend` that enforces this on TCP port `80`. Pods in `storage` must no longer be able to reach `api`.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: api-allow-frontend
      namespace: backend
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: api
      policyTypes:
      - Ingress
      ingress:
      - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              tier: frontend
        ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 80

A `namespaceSelector` on its own allows every pod in matching namespaces. Combine `namespaceSelector` and `podSelector` in the *same* list item to require both (a `-` before each makes them alternatives instead). Verify with `kubectl -n storage exec deploy/db -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 api.backend` (times out) and the same from `frontend` (works).

references.title: Network Policies — behavior of to and from selectors

checks.name: api-allow-frontend
checks.hint: api-allow-frontend must select app=api pods and be an Ingress policy
frontend pods must still reach the api service
storage pods must be blocked from the api service

questions.title: Block the cloud metadata endpoint
questions.text:
Pods in namespace `frontend` must not be able to reach the cloud metadata service at `169.254.169.254`, while all other egress stays allowed.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `deny-metadata` in `frontend` that applies to **all** pods in the namespace and allows egress to everywhere (`0.0.0.0/0`) **except** `169.254.169.254/32`.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: deny-metadata
      namespace: frontend
    spec:
      podSelector: {}
      policyTypes:
      - Egress
      egress:
      - to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
            except:
            - 169.254.169.254/32

`ipBlock.except` carves holes out of an allowed CIDR. Because this policy allows everything else, in-cluster traffic and DNS keep working.

checks.name: deny-metadata
checks.hint: deny-metadata must select all pods, be an Egress policy, and allow 0.0.0.0/0 except 169.254.169.254/32

questions.title: Verify platform binaries
questions.text:
Release binaries were downloaded to `/opt/bin/` on the base host together with the published checksum file `/opt/bin/SHA256SUMS`.

Verify the binaries. Exactly one has been tampered with — write its **file name only** to `/opt/answers/tampered.txt`.
questions.solution:
cd /opt/bin
    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
    # kubectl: OK
    # kubeadm: OK
    # kubelet: FAILED
    echo kubelet > /opt/answers/tampered.txt

`sha256sum -c` recomputes each hash and compares it with the listed value; a single changed byte changes the whole digest. Always verify downloads against the checksums published by the Kubernetes release page before installing them on nodes.

checks.hint: /opt/answers/tampered.txt must contain the name of the binary whose checksum fails

questions.title: Upgrade a worker node
questions.text:
The control plane of cluster `cks` runs `v1.31.2` but worker `cks2-node2` is still on `v1.31.0`, which has known vulnerabilities.

Upgrade the node to `v1.31.2` (kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl). Drain it first and make it schedulable again afterwards. It must report `v1.31.2` and `Ready`.
questions.solution:
kubectl drain cks2-node2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
    ssh cks2-node2
    sudo -i
    apt-mark unhold kubeadm && apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.31.2-1.1 && apt-mark hold kubeadm
    kubeadm upgrade node
    apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && apt-get install -y kubelet=1.31.2-1.1 kubectl=1.31.2-1.1 && apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl
    systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
    exit; exit
    kubectl uncordon cks2-node2
    kubectl get nodes

Workers use `kubeadm upgrade node` (not `apply`); the version shown by `kubectl get nodes` is the running kubelet's, so it only changes after the restart.

checks.hint: cks2-node2 kubelet must report v1.31.2
cks2-node2 is still cordoned
cks2-node2 is not Ready

questions.title: Restrict a user's access
questions.text:
The user `dev-bob` is bound to `cluster-admin` through the ClusterRoleBinding `bob-admin`.

Remove that binding and instead give `dev-bob` read-only access (the built-in ClusterRole `view`) in namespace `frontend` only, via a RoleBinding named `bob-view`.
questions.solution:
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding bob-admin
    kubectl -n frontend create rolebinding bob-view --clusterrole=view --user=dev-bob
    kubectl auth can-i list pods -n frontend --as dev-bob     # yes
    kubectl auth can-i delete pods -n frontend --as dev-bob   # no
    kubectl auth can-i list pods -n backend --as dev-bob      # no

A RoleBinding can reference a ClusterRole; that reuses the role's rules but scopes them to the binding's namespace.

checks.name: bob-admin
checks.hint: clusterrolebinding bob-admin still exists

checks.name: bob-view
checks.hint: rolebinding bob-view in frontend must bind ClusterRole view to user dev-bob
dev-bob must be able to list pods in frontend
dev-bob must not be able to delete pods
dev-bob must have no access in backend

questions.title: Minimize the host footprint
questions.text:
Node `cks2-node1` runs services that have no business on a Kubernetes worker: `apache2` and `telnetd`.

Stop both and make sure they do not start on boot. Leave the kubelet and container runtime alone.
questions.solution:
ssh cks2-node1
    sudo -i
    systemctl list-units --type=service      # or: systemctl status apache2 telnetd
    systemctl disable --now apache2
    systemctl disable --now telnetd
    systemctl is-active apache2 telnetd       # inactive
    exit; exit

Every extra listening service on a node is attack surface; `disable --now` stops the unit and removes it from the boot targets in one step. `apt-get remove` would go one step further.

checks.name: apache2
checks.hint: apache2 must be stopped and disabled on cks2-node1

checks.name: telnetd
checks.hint: telnetd must be stopped and disabled on cks2-node1

checks.name: kubelet
checks.hint: the kubelet must keep running

questions.title: Kubelet CIS settings
questions.text:
`kube-bench` reports failing kubelet checks on node `cks2-node1`: the read-only port is enabled and kernel defaults are not protected.

Fix `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` so that `readOnlyPort` is `0` and `protectKernelDefaults` is `true`, restart the kubelet, and confirm the node stays `Ready`.
questions.solution:
ssh cks2-node1
    sudo -i
    kube-bench                                   # [FAIL] 4.2.4, [FAIL] 4.2.6
    vim /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
      # readOnlyPort: 0
      # protectKernelDefaults: true
    systemctl restart kubelet
    kube-bench --check 4.2.4,4.2.6               # PASS
    exit; exit
    kubectl get nodes

The read-only port (10255) exposes pod and node information without authentication; `protectKernelDefaults` makes the kubelet refuse to start if kernel tunables are not in the expected secure state.

checks.hint: kubelet config must set readOnlyPort: 0
kubelet config must set protectKernelDefaults: true

checks.name: kubelet
checks.hint: kubelet on cks2-node1 is not running
cks2-node1 is not Ready

questions.title: Default seccomp for a Deployment
questions.text: Make every container of the Deployment `ui` in namespace `frontend` run with the container runtime's default seccomp profile, set at the **pod** level, and run as a non-root user (`runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 1000`). The Deployment must stay available.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n frontend edit deployment ui

    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          securityContext:
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000

    kubectl -n frontend rollout status deployment ui

`RuntimeDefault` applies containerd's built-in profile, which blocks a few dozen dangerous syscalls at no operational cost. The pod-level securityContext is inherited by every container unless a container overrides it.

references.title: Restrict a Container's Syscalls with seccomp
Configure a Security Context for a Pod

checks.name: ui
checks.hint: ui pod template must set seccompProfile RuntimeDefault, runAsNonRoot true and runAsUser 1000 at pod level

checks.name: ui
checks.hint: deployment ui is not fully available

questions.title: Pod Security Standards: baseline
questions.text:
Namespace `storage` must enforce the `baseline` Pod Security Standard and additionally **warn** about `restricted` violations.

Apply the labels, then fix the Deployment `legacy-agent` in that namespace, which currently uses host PID namespace sharing, so that its pods are admitted and the Deployment becomes available.
questions.solution:
kubectl label namespace storage pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=restricted
    kubectl -n storage get deployment legacy-agent -o yaml | grep hostPID
    kubectl -n storage edit deployment legacy-agent      # delete the hostPID: true line
    kubectl -n storage rollout status deployment legacy-agent

`baseline` blocks the well-known privilege escalations (host namespaces, privileged, hostPath, most added capabilities) while allowing ordinary workloads; `warn` surfaces what would break under `restricted` without enforcing it yet.

references.title: Enforce Pod Security Standards with namespace labels

checks.name: storage
checks.hint: namespace storage must carry enforce=baseline and warn=restricted labels

checks.name: legacy-agent
checks.hint: legacy-agent must not use hostPID

checks.name: legacy-agent
checks.hint: legacy-agent pods are not all available

questions.title: Encrypt Secrets at rest
questions.text:
Configure the API server on `cks2-control` to encrypt Secrets at rest:

- create `/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml` with an `EncryptionConfiguration` that uses an `aescbc` key for `secrets` (with `identity` as the fallback provider)
- pass it to the API server with `--encryption-provider-config=/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml`

The API server must come back healthy.
questions.solution:
ssh cks2-control
    sudo -i
    mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/enc
    head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64      # in this lab, any 32-byte base64 string works
    vim /etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml

    apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
    kind: EncryptionConfiguration
    resources:
    - resources:
      - secrets
      providers:
      - aescbc:
          keys:
          - name: key1
            secret: c2VjcmV0LWtleS1mb3ItdGhlLWxhYi1lbnZpcm9ubWVudA==
      - identity: {}

    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
      # add:  - --encryption-provider-config=/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml
      # and mount /etc/kubernetes/enc into the container (hostPath volume + volumeMount, readOnly)
    exit; exit
    kubectl get nodes
    # then re-write existing secrets so they are stored encrypted:
    # kubectl get secrets -A -o json | kubectl replace -f -

Provider order matters: the first provider encrypts new writes; `identity` last lets the server still read old, unencrypted data.

checks.hint: /etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml must be an EncryptionConfiguration
the configuration must use an aescbc provider
the configuration must apply to secrets
kube-apiserver needs --encryption-provider-config=/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml
the kube-apiserver manifest is broken

questions.title: Use the internal registry
questions.text:
Company policy requires all production images to come from `registry.internal.corp`. The Deployment `store` in namespace `shop` still pulls `docker.io/acme/store:2.1`.

Switch it to `registry.internal.corp/shop/store:2.1` and make sure the rollout completes.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n shop set image deployment/store main=registry.internal.corp/shop/store:2.1
    kubectl -n shop rollout status deployment store

In a real cluster an admission control (ImagePolicyWebhook, or a policy engine such as Kyverno/Gatekeeper) enforces the allowed registries so this cannot regress.

checks.hint: store must use registry.internal.corp/shop/store:2.1

questions.title: Count vulnerabilities
questions.text: Scan the image used by Deployment `api` in namespace `backend` with `trivy` and write the number of **HIGH** severity vulnerabilities (the number only) to `/opt/answers/api-high.txt` on the base host.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n backend get deployment api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'   # httpd:2.4
    trivy image --severity HIGH httpd:2.4      # Total: 4 (HIGH: 4)
    echo 4 > /opt/answers/api-high.txt

checks.hint: /opt/answers/api-high.txt must contain the HIGH count for httpd:2.4

questions.title: Pin an image by digest
questions.text:
Deployment `ui` in namespace `frontend` references `nginx:1.27` by tag. Tags are mutable; pin the image to this immutable digest instead:

    nginx@sha256:5ed8fcc66f4ed123c1b2560ed708dc54c5a84f8b28a9e5b7a5e8e4d3b6e7f4a1

The Deployment must remain available.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n frontend set image deployment/ui main=nginx@sha256:5ed8fcc66f4ed123c1b2560ed708dc54c5a84f8b28a9e5b7a5e8e4d3b6e7f4a1
    kubectl -n frontend rollout status deployment ui

A digest identifies exact image content; a re-pushed tag cannot silently change what runs. Get a running image's digest with `kubectl get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}'`.

checks.name: ui
checks.hint: ui must reference the given digest

checks.name: ui
checks.hint: deployment ui is not fully available

questions.title: Audit log forensics
questions.text:
The Secret `payroll` in namespace `finance` was deleted. API server audit logs are on `cks2-control` at `/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log`.

Find the username of the principal that deleted it and write it (exactly, nothing else) to `/opt/answers/deleter.txt` on the base host.
questions.solution:
ssh cks2-control
    sudo grep payroll /var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log | grep '"verb":"delete"'
    # ... "user":{"username":"mallory@corp.local" ...
    exit
    echo mallory@corp.local > /opt/answers/deleter.txt

Each audit line is one JSON event: `verb`, `user.username`, `objectRef` and `responseStatus` answer who did what to which object and whether it succeeded. Filter by object first, then by verb.

checks.hint: /opt/answers/deleter.txt must contain the username that deleted the secret

questions.title: Crypto miner detected
questions.text:
Falco on node `cks2-node1` has raised `Detect crypto miners using the Stratum protocol` alerts for a workload in namespace `backend`.

Identify which Deployment the offending container belongs to and **delete** that Deployment.
questions.solution:
ssh cks2-node1
    sudo journalctl -u falco --no-pager | grep -i stratum
    # ... k8s.ns=backend k8s.pod=metrics-agent-... image=docker.io/acme/metrics:1.4 command=xmrig ...
    exit
    kubectl -n backend get deployments -o wide
    kubectl -n backend delete deployment metrics-agent

Scaling to zero would stop the miner too, but a compromised image should be removed and rebuilt from a trusted source rather than kept around.

checks.name: metrics-agent
checks.hint: deployment metrics-agent (image docker.io/acme/metrics:1.4) must be deleted

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api must remain

questions.title: Remove dangerous pod settings
questions.text:
The Deployment `cache` in namespace `backend` runs a privileged container and mounts the host's Docker socket.

Remove the privileged flag and the `/var/run/docker.sock` hostPath mount, and set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` on the container. The Deployment must remain available.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n backend edit deployment cache
      # delete:  privileged: true
      # delete the docker-sock volume and its volumeMount
      # add under the container's securityContext:  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    kubectl -n backend rollout status deployment cache

A container with the Docker/containerd socket mounted can start privileged containers on the host — it is root on the node. Combined with `privileged: true` there is no isolation left at all.

checks.name: cache
checks.hint: cache must not be privileged, must not mount /var/run/docker.sock, and must set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

checks.name: cache
checks.hint: deployment cache is not available

questions.title: Dedicated ServiceAccount with least privilege
questions.text: The Deployment `api` in namespace `backend` runs as the `default` ServiceAccount. Create a ServiceAccount `api-sa` in `backend`, a Role `cm-reader` allowing only `get` and `list` on `configmaps`, and a RoleBinding `api-sa-cm` binding them. Then make the Deployment use `api-sa`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n backend create serviceaccount api-sa
    kubectl -n backend create role cm-reader --verb=get,list --resource=configmaps
    kubectl -n backend create rolebinding api-sa-cm --role=cm-reader --serviceaccount=backend:api-sa
    kubectl -n backend set serviceaccount deployment api api-sa
    kubectl -n backend rollout status deployment api
    kubectl -n backend auth can-i list secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:backend:api-sa   # no

The `default` ServiceAccount is shared by every pod in the namespace; giving it permissions gives them to everything. A per-workload account keeps the blast radius of a compromised pod small.

checks.name: api-sa
checks.hint: serviceaccount api-sa missing in backend
api-sa must be able to get configmaps
api-sa must not be able to list secrets

checks.name: api
checks.hint: deployment api must run as serviceaccount api-sa
